newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB's problem loans may above its estimate -- paper.
newsitem.headline: NCB's problem loans may above its estimate -- paper.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) has an estimated 700 billion yen in loans which may not be collected, above the bank's original estimate of 500 billion yen, a Japanese business daily said on Tuedsay.
Other financial institutions, however, are likely to agree to cooperate in NCB's restucturing, Nihon Keizai Shimbun said.
The paper said the higher figure for the problem loans was revealed in an investigation conducted by the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
MOF's findings also indicated that NCB's write-offs of bad debts in the year to March 31, 1997, were "reasonable", the paper said.
NCB has disclosed the contents of MOF's findings to other financial institutions, hoping to convince them to assist its restructuring by buying new NCB shares, the paper said.
Other financial institutions are expected to decide whether or not they will buy the new NCB shares later this week, the paper said, adding that they are likely to agree to do so.
An NCB spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
